title: The Same Mark
description: A plumb-bob hanging inside a square. You have now seen it in two places that have nothing to do with each other.

two_places.title: Two places
two_places.objective: Nothing to do about it. Keep your eyes open.
two_places.journal: A plumb-bob hanging inside a square, cut or stamped or painted. I have seen it twice now, in two places that have no business sharing anything. It is probably a maker's mark. Most things are.

asked_the_chainman.title: Ask the man who paints them
asked_the_chainman.objective: Alder Pyke walks lines for whoever is paying. Ask him what the mark is.
asked_the_chainman.journal: There is an old chainman on Granary Row with a hundred feet of chain over his shoulder and a plumb-bob in his pocket, and the plumb-bob has the mark stamped on the flat. He paints them. He has painted a great many.

started_counting.title: Counting them
started_counting.journal: It is a survey mark. Pyke was quite clear and quite bored: a chain is dragged, a line is walked, a mark is painted, and a man is paid one and threepence a day for it. There is nothing to it. I have started writing down where I see them anyway, and I could not tell you why.

let_it_alone.title: A maker's mark
let_it_alone.journal: It is a survey mark. Somebody is measuring something, which is what people with money do before they buy it, and it is no more sinister than a milestone. I asked, I was answered, and I have let it alone.
